summary: Careful, well‑documented preregistered paired study comparing one‑shot vs verifier‑assisted NL→config pipelines. Execution and archival artifacts are comprehensive; the disclosed analytic deviation (Wilcoxon → exact McNemar for binary outcomes) is documented and justified. Results (n=1,199 pairs) show near‑ceiling baseline performance and no statistically significant verifier benefit. Manuscript is reproducible and limitations are acknowledged.
optional_revisions: Add a single sentence quantitatively tying the preregistered power target (5 pp MDE) to the observed near‑ceiling baseline (e.g., note that the preregistered design targeted a 5‑percentage‑point improvement and that the observed CI and discordant counts imply the study was underpowered to detect much smaller absolute gains), referencing archived CI and contingency artifacts.

Briefly note in the Limitations that synthetic task design choices likely reduced baseline difficulty (point to task_manifest examples) and so the low repair invocation count likely reflects corpus design as well as validator settings; this helps readers interpret generalizability.
